tasks.gr11-oop-classes-objects-t1: Topic: OOP — Classes and Objects. Cover the concept of a class as a blueprint defining attributes (instance variables) and methods, the distinction between a class and an object (instance), UML class diagram notation (three sections: class name, attributes, methods), naming conventions (PascalCase for classes, camelCase for attributes), encapsulation (private attributes, public getters/setters), and instantiating objects using the constructor. Ask Grade 11 learners to identify class vs object, read UML diagrams, explain encapsulation, trace object creation code, and distinguish between class-level and instance-level members.
tasks.gr11-oop-methods-constructors-t1: Topic: OOP — Methods and Constructors. Cover constructors as special methods that initialise object state when an object is created, default vs parameterised constructors, the role of `this` (Delphi: `Self`) to refer to the current object, procedure methods (no return value) vs function methods (return a value), method signatures (name + parameters), and calling methods on objects. Ask Grade 11 learners to write or complete constructors, trace method calls through objects, distinguish procedures from functions, and explain why constructors have no return type.
tasks.gr11-algorithms-t1: Topic: Advanced Algorithms. Cover algorithm design for more complex problems (nested loops, multiple conditions), the bubble sort algorithm (compare adjacent elements, swap if out of order, repeat until no swaps), the linear (sequential) search algorithm, the binary search algorithm (sorted array, halving the search space), and procedural decomposition (breaking a problem into subproblems / subroutines). Ask Grade 11 learners to trace bubble sort steps on a small array, determine how many comparisons binary search needs, write pseudocode for a search, and identify which algorithm is more efficient for a given scenario.
tasks.gr11-file-handling-t1: Topic: File Handling. Cover the difference between text files (human-readable, plain text lines) and binary files (machine format), the file-access modes: read, write (overwrite), append, opening and closing files explicitly to avoid data loss or corruption, reading line-by-line vs reading the entire file, writing strings to a file, and appending new records without destroying existing data. Ask Grade 11 learners to complete file-processing code snippets, predict file contents after write/append operations, identify the correct mode for a scenario, and spot common file-handling errors (not closing a file, opening in wrong mode).
